en.title: Bass X Machina: First 5 Minutes Reveal Steampunk Western's Bloody Opening
en.summary: Netflix's upcoming anime series Bass X Machina dropped its electrifying first five minutes at Anime NYC, showcasing a brutal bounty hunter in a steampunk western world. Executive producer Brian Tyree Henry shared insights into the kinetic action and unique blend of genres.
en.body:
The highly anticipated anime series **Bass X Machina** gave fans an exclusive, action-packed preview at Anime NYC, revealing the show's gritty steampunk western aesthetic and its formidable protagonist. The first five minutes, shown to an excited crowd, immediately plunged viewers into a visually stunning and violent world, setting a high bar for what's to come.

Executive producer and star **Brian Tyree Henry** took the stage to discuss the series, co-created by **LeSean Thomas** (known for **Cannon Busters** and **Yasuke**) and produced by **Studio Mir** (the powerhouse behind **Devil May Cry** and **Skull Island**). **Bass X Machina** reimagines the legendary story of Bass Reeves, the first Black U.S. Marshal, casting him as a slick, deadly bounty hunter navigating a dangerous frontier filled with outlaws, colossal war machines, and supernatural threats. The preview footage delivered on this promise with a dazzling, high-octane sequence.

## A Brutal Introduction to Bass Reeves

The opening moments depicted a snow-swept landscape where Bass Reeves, his face obscured by a cloth, expertly pursues a speeding train. The train has been hijacked by a mob of criminals who have already graphically dispatched the security detail in pursuit of a gold shipment. Reeves boards the train with cold precision, demanding the outlaws disarm. When one criminal foolishly draws a weapon, Reeves swiftly and brutally eliminates everyone except his intended target, revealing that his quarry is one of two twin brothers. The stunned twin's exclamation, "But you're a lawman," is met with Reeves' chilling retort, "Not a lawman. Bounty hunter," immediately establishing his morally ambiguous and lethal nature within this unique world.

## What This Means for Series Fans

This explosive introduction is precisely the kind of kinetic, character-driven action that fans of **LeSean Thomas** and **Studio Mir** have come to expect. The steampunk western fusion is a bold creative choice, promising a visually distinct experience that blends historical inspiration with fantastical elements. The early reveal of Reeves' bounty hunter persona, rather than a traditional lawman, suggests a narrative that will explore darker themes and complex motivations. For viewers who crave intricate world-building and unflinching action sequences, **Bass X Machina** is shaping up to be a must-watch series that offers a fresh perspective on a historical figure through a hyper-stylized lens.

## What's Next

While a specific release date for **Bass X Machina** has not yet been announced, this tantalizing glimpse suggests production is well underway. Fans can anticipate more details and potential further previews as Netflix gears up for the series' eventual launch on the platform.

content_raw: Picture Credit: Netflix At the top of Netflix’s premiere showcase at Anime NYC, the excited crowd at the Main Stage room was given an exclusive look into Bass X Machina with none other than executive producer and star Brian Tyree Henry. Henry took the stage alongside panel host Straw Hat Goofy for a detailed discussion about the series and its production process. Created by LeSean Thomas ( Cannon Busters , Yasuke ) and produced by Studio Mir ( Devil May Cry , Skull Island ), Bass X Machina is a steampunk western infused with the legendary story of Bass Reeves, the first Black U.S. Marshal. In this gritty, hyper‑stylized, kinetic action series, Reeves operates as a cool and slick bounty hunter in a realm full of homicidal outlaws, enormous war machines, and even supernatural terrors. Here is a complete breakdown of everything revealed during the presentation, including details from the series’ footage (see here if you missed our news coverage of just the trailer ): The First Five Minutes Fans were treated to the first five minutes of the series in a high‑octane, dazzling, and bloody sequence. The footage opens in a wintry setting with Bass Reeves on a speedy horse, pursuing a train. A mob of criminals has hijacked and robbed a cart full of gold, with the slain security graphically deceased on the ground. Bass leaps onboard, face covered with cloth and eyes as cold as the air. He suggests the criminals disarm and surrender, as he’s looking for a wanted man. When one pulls out his gun, Bass quickly head‑shots everyone except his target. It also appears that the man he’s looking for is one of the twin brothers. “But you’re a lawman,” one of the twins says, shocked. “Not a lawman. Bounty hunter,” he responds. Both twins suggest they’re triplets, claiming his target isn’t in the room. They both try to get the jump on Bass at once. An exterior shot of the train passes with only two gunshots heard in quick succession. Cut back to the cart, and both brothers lie dead on the ground. The third brother slides open the door and tries to flee. On a cart full of criminals and innocent passengers, a shootout erupts. Concerned about a mother and child in fear and other casualties, Bass cautiously takes out the adversaries. A man touches his shoulder to thank him, but Bass flashes over an ominous past regarding his reconstruction, similar to Wolverine’s traumatic Weapon X flashbacks. He pulls out a gun on him, before regaining his sanity. He pursues the last brother into a cart where he sets off a nine‑barreled machine gun, laughing maniacally.
